description: `nonUndefined(value)` is the same test as `!isUndefined(value)`, written so that a guard clause reads as a sentence rather than as a negation.
The test is `typeof value === "undefined"`, which is safe for a variable that was never declared, unlike a bare comparison.
`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).
returns: `true` when the value is not `undefined`; otherwise `false`.

examples.title: What passes and what does not
examples.body:
```javascript
nonUndefined(null); // => true
nonUndefined(0); // => true
nonUndefined(""); // => true
nonUndefined(undefined); // => false
```
